newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Feb 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Feb 18.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on February 18. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The government-backed chairman of Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) Surjadi said the general elections in May would experience a set back if there were too many rules regulating it. The election commission has said it will screen the speeches to be broadcast by the contesting parties on the state-owned television network TVRI.

Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd has teamed up with U.S. giant Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc to develop the huge Busang gold find in East Kalimantan. Indonesia will own 40 percent of the jont venture, Bre-X 45 percent and Freeport 15 percent.

Assistant to the army chief of staff for security affairs Major-General Zacky Anwar Makarim has confirmed that about 300 people have been killed during the ethnic riots between the native Dayak and the Maduran in West Kalimantan province since December.

Japanese media correspondents have received a warning from the Indonesian government about their coverage of recent riots in Indonesia. The letter alleged the Japanese correspondents have been used by certain groups who did not wish to see Indonesia progress.
